question: What will the series score of the 2026 ALCS be after Game 4 (October 16)?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 80 best-of-seven LCS 1985-2025: 11 sweeps (13.75%), 20 at 4-1, 27 at 4-2, 22 at 4-3. Converting final results to after-Game-4 states under random game ordering (4-2 series: 40% were 3-1/60% 2-2; 4-3 series: 40%/60%) gives ~49.5% 3-1, ~36.75% 2-2, ~13.75% sweep, consistent with coin-flip theory (50/37.5/12.5) plus mild favorite strength. ALCS teams not yet set; Rays lead NYY 2-0 and White Sox lead CLE 2-0 in ALDS; a Rays (league-best) vs underdog matchup would slightly raise sweep odds. Market check: no Kalshi/Polymarket/Manifold/bookmaker market on series state after Game 4 found; only AL pennant markets (Rays ~30%, Yankees ~22%, ~$9M volume) which are a different contract and only inform team-strength asymmetry.

- Theory: equal teams p=0.5 gives 3-1 50%, 2-2 37.5%, 4-0 12.5%; p=0.57 favorite gives sweep ~14%, 2-2 ~35%.
- Not found: actual game-by-game after-G4 state for each historical LCS (conversion is modeled, not counted); any market on exact series state/length for 2026 ALCS (none on Kalshi/Polymarket/Manifold/bookmakers in searches).

Empirical best-of-seven sweep rate ~17% (FanGraphs, 27/158, 1903-2012) and ~15% in LCS since 1985 by my count; MLB.com cites 27 LCS/WS series tied 2-2 since 1985 (~29% of such series), a bit below the binomial. Blend: 2-2 35%, 3-1 50%, 4-0 15%. Possible Rays-White Sox mismatch nudges sweeps/3-1 slightly up.
